summary: This article pays tribute to the local volunteers and groups who protect and improve neighborhood parks. It profiles ten initiatives from September 2023 to April 2024, covering cleanups, solar-powered bins, photography, tree planting, accessibility, outdoor education, stream cleaning, pollinator gardens and a park-based fitness program. Each is led by a named community member who explains their motivation.
one_line: A profile of ten community-led initiatives and the volunteers who clean, green, and make neighborhood parks more inclusive and sustainable.
key_facts: The Green Brigade began weekly cleanup drives in Miller Park on September 5, 2023; it was founded by retired school teacher Sarah McKinley and now has over 40 volunteers.
Sarah McKinley says, "Our parks are the lungs of the city."
On October 12, 2023, Miller Park became the first in the region to introduce solar-powered waste bins, an initiative spearheaded by tech enthusiast Arjun Patel.
Arjun Patel's solar compactor bins reduce the frequency of waste collection, cut carbon emissions and teach the public about solar energy; he plans to expand solar use to other park facilities.

Photographer Emma Langley's ongoing project 'Seasons of the Park' documents the parks through the changing seasons; her work has been shown at City Hall and local galleries, with proceeds going to conservation.
On November 24, 2023, the high school ecoclub 'Sprouts of Change', led by sixteen-year-old Zoey Thompson, planted over 200 trees in and around Robinson Park.

David Kim and his team launched 'Parks for All' on December 15, 2023, redesigning park entryways and pathways and installing assistive facilities for people with disabilities; Kim was inspired by his sister, who uses a wheelchair.
Maria Gonzalez, a former science teacher, held the first 'Nature's Classroom' event on January 21, 2024, and runs weekly outdoor classes on local flora and fauna in Grandview Park.
The Stream Clean Team was formed on February 18, 2024, by twin siblings James and Jenna Foster and holds monthly cleanups of the waterways in Northside Park.
Since March 29, 2024, Pollinator Pals, led by gardener Lara Nguyen, has turned sections of Fairview Park into pollinator gardens using native species.
Fitness coach Tom Bennett started the Green Gym on April 6, 2024, combining workouts with park maintenance activities.
The Green Gym has inspired similar initiatives in neighboring communities.
